subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Pneumatic Conveying: Moving Materials by Air
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pneumatic Conveying: Moving Materials by Air usable.

hook.text: Grain elevators move tons of wheat through pipes using airflow alone. A fan and a tube replace belts and buckets.

buildup.text: A blower pushes air through a pipe. Material enters the stream and rides along. A separator at the end catches the product.

discovery.text: Dilute-phase systems use fast air to suspend particles. Dense-phase uses pressure pulses to push slugs through the pipe.

twist.text: Enclosed pipes mean no dust, no spills, no contamination. Food and pharma plants choose pneumatic conveying for cleanliness.

climax.text: Cement plants, flour mills, and plastics factories all move bulk materials this way. Air does the heavy lifting.

punchline.text: Blow air through a pipe. The material follows. No belts, no mess.

quiz.question: Why do food and pharmaceutical plants prefer pneumatic conveying?
options: It moves material faster than any belt or bucket system
Enclosed pipes eliminate dust, spillage, and contamination
It uses less energy than mechanical conveyors
